program: SNAP — Idaho DHW's own consumer pages use plain "SNAP" (formerly Food Stamps); the administrative code's own title is "Idaho Food Stamp Program" (IDAPA 16.03.04), see PROVENANCE.md
agency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (DHW), Self-Reliance Programs division
agency_short: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare (DHW)
admin_note: Idaho is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program (no county option-in like CA/NY/MN/WI/VA) — DHW's Self-Reliance Programs division administers directly through field offices statewide, with no county-level policy variation. GENUINE FLAGSHIP CORRECTION this pack found: several secondary/aggregator sources (and this pack's own preliminary search synthesis) describe Idaho's Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) as having "no resource limit," claiming a car's value "does not affect eligibility." Idaho's own administrative code directly contradicts this: IDAPA 16.03.04.010.09 defines BBCE households as "also subject to resource, gross, and net income eligibility standards" — NOT exempt — and IDAPA 16.03.04.305 sets that BBCE resource limit at a flat five thousand dollars ($5,000), independently confirmed on DHW's own consumer-facing Apply for SNAP page ("For most households, resources must be under $5,000 to qualify for SNAP"). This is a real, elevated limit above the plain federal $3,000/$4,500 baseline (available to non-BBCE households per FNS-published figures), but it is a limit, not a waiver — a true asset-test waiver in Idaho is reserved for the narrower Categorical Eligibility (CE) pathway (all household members receiving TAFI/AABD/SSI, IDAPA 178), which IS fully exempt from resource, gross, and net income standards. SEPARATE TIME-SENSITIVE FLAGSHIP FINDING: Idaho's SNAP candy-and-soda purchase restriction (approved under Idaho House Bill 109, effective February 15, 2026) was NOT among the waivers vacated by the June 22, 2026 federal court order in Aragon et al. v. Rollins et al. (that order struck down Colorado's, Iowa's, Nebraska's, Tennessee's, and West Virginia's food-restriction waivers specifically) — Idaho's own retailer-facing page, last updated April 27, 2026 (five weeks after the court order), describes the restriction as actively in force with no medical exemptions, and secondary reporting corroborates Idaho state officials asserting the ruling does not apply to them since Idaho was not a party to that suit. Confirm current operative practice with DHW directly before treating either finding as permanently settled, the same caution this roster already carries for CA/NY/MN/WI/OH/NC/NJ/VA/GA/IN/TN/MO/MD/CO/SC/AL/LA/KY/OK/CT/NE.
system: DHW's Self-Reliance Programs division processes SNAP centrally through field offices (no county offices with independent policy authority); applicants apply online through Idalink (idalink.idaho.gov, DHW's self-service portal covering SNAP, Medicaid, cash, and child care assistance in one account), by phone or in person through DHW's toll-free line (1-877-456-1233) and closest field office, or by mail/email/fax (Self-Reliance Programs, PO Box 83720, Boise, ID 83720-0026; MyBenefits@dhw.idaho.gov; fax 1-866-434-8278). An interview (face-to-face or telephone) is required with every application and, per IDAPA 16.03.04.120, must recur at least once every 24 months for households certified for a 24-month period, and every 12 months for all other households — this pack flags the underlying certification-period LENGTHS themselves (which households qualify for a 24-month vs. shorter certification) as lower-confidence, see freshness.json.
